findings.source_quote: τὰ δὲ ἐδέσματα ἃ ἔπεμψεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ δείπνου, αἱ ἐντολαί εἰσιν ἃς ἔδωκε τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ
findings.english_quote: The food sent from the dinner is the commandments he gave his people through his Son.
findings.issue: The passive compression drops the explicit recipient, αὐτῷ, and no longer expresses the source's sending action as something he did. The recipient is part of the parable's correspondence, not merely dispensable sentence complexity.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “The food he sent to him from the dinner is the commandments he gave his people through his Son.”

findings.source_quote: αὕτη οὖν ἡ σάρξ, ἐν ᾗ κατῴκησε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἐδούλευσε τῷ πνεύματι καλῶς
findings.english_quote: This flesh served the Spirit well.
findings.issue: The simplified edition omits the relative clause explicitly identifying this flesh as that in which the Holy Spirit dwelt. Although the preceding sentence describes God's causing the Spirit to dwell in flesh, the source here repeats and affirms that indwelling while identifying the flesh that served. The earlier statement does not provide complete coverage of this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “So this flesh, in which the Holy Spirit dwelt, served the Spirit well.”

summary: The standard edition faithfully covers the selected working Greek and accurately discloses the supplied reports of conjectures, restorations, variants, and physical losses. Its disputed negative and difficult Spirit/flesh and reward assertions should remain. Independent review of the simplified edition identifies two clause-level omissions requiring revision. Both editions follow reader-facing servant terminology. This assessment evaluates the supplied source and attributed evidence reports; it does not authenticate unseen images, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
